proof.text: Let $A\subseteq S$ be an affine open. Pull the singleton fpqc covering $X\to S$ and the descent datum $(V,\varphi)$ back along $A\to S$. By [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change] the first projection $X_A=A\times_SX\to A$ is again a singleton fpqc covering, and hypothesis (1) preserves $\mathcal P$ for the pulled-back morphism $V_A\to X_A$. It therefore suffices to construct an effective descent of this pulled-back datum for every affine open $A$; the descended objects and their transition maps will be glued in Step 4. (Source: the general-base part of Lemma 02W3, after the affine case.)

proof.text: Fix an affine open $A\subseteq S$. By [lem-galois-fpqc-singleton-affine-refinement] choose a finite coproduct $X'_A=\coprod_jX_j$ of affine opens of $X_A$, a map $h_A:X'_A\to X_A$, and a flat surjective morphism $g_A:X'_A\to A$ with $g_A=(X_A\to A)\circ h_A$. Pulling the datum back along $h_A$ preserves $\mathcal P$ by hypothesis (1). Hypothesis (3), applied to the affine flat surjective morphism $g_A$, produces a scheme $W_A\to A$ and an isomorphism $\psi'_A:W_A\times_AX'_A\xrightarrow{\sim}V_A\times_{X_A}X'_A$ compatible with the pulled-back descent data.

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02W3, proof lines 9070-9091: refine an affine-base covering by a finite standard affine covering, form its coproduct, and apply hypothesis (3)

proof.text: The datum on $W_A\times_AX_A$ and the datum on $V_A$ have pullbacks to $X'_A$ identified by $\psi'_A$. The refinement map $h_A:X'_A\to X_A$ is a refinement of singleton fpqc coverings, so [lem-galois-fpqc-refinement-fully-faithful] descends $\psi'_A$ uniquely to an isomorphism $\psi_A:W_A\times_AX_A\xrightarrow{\sim}V_A$ over $X_A$ satisfying $\varphi_A\circ\mathrm{pr}_0^*\psi_A=\mathrm{pr}_1^*\psi_A\circ\mathrm{can}_{W_A}$. Thus the pulled-back descent datum is effective over every affine open $A$.

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02W3, proof lines 9078-9088: the pullback functor along a refinement is fully faithful (Lemma 02W0), so effectiveness over the refinement descends

proof.text: For affine opens $B\subseteq A\subseteq S$, compare the two effective data over $B$: $(W_B,\psi_B)$ and $(W_A\times_AB,\psi_A|_B)$. Their pullbacks to the singleton fpqc cover $X_B\to B$ are canonically isomorphic through $\psi_B$ and the restriction of $\psi_A$. By [lem-galois-fpqc-morphisms-descend] this gives a unique transition morphism $\rho^A_B:W_B\to W_A$ over $B$; uniqueness gives $\rho^A_A=\mathrm{id}$ and $\rho^A_C=\rho^A_B\circ\rho^B_C$. The same argument applied to inverse isomorphisms shows that $\rho^A_B$ identifies $W_B$ with the inverse image of $B$ in $W_A$. The relative gluing leaf [lem-weil-pbc-relative-glueing-affine-opens] therefore supplies a scheme $W\to S$ with $W\times_SA\cong W_A$. The maps $\psi_A$ agree on overlaps by the same uniqueness argument, so [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] glues them to an isomorphism $\psi:W\times_SX\xrightarrow{\sim}V$; the local compatibility equations glue as well. Taking $U=W$ proves the conclusion.
